samples.summary: Design doc still documents the removed "warn-and-skip without CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN" contract for `spec-to-pr.mjs review`
samples.evidence: `docs/design/harness-engineering.md:2403-2406` reads: "**Local review is a convenience, not authority:** `spec-to-pr.mjs review` runs the same lenses over the working diff, but needs `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` and degrades to a warn-and-skip when it is absent. The authoritative panel is still the cloud one". This change deletes exactly that early return (`scripts/agent/spec-to-pr.mjs:865` now only warns via `ambientAuthNotice` and proceeds on the logged-in session), and its own docblock argues the opposite — that for a non-`agent/`, non-`agent:managed` branch the local round is the ONLY machine review. `CLAUDE.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `.claude/commands/spec-to-pr.md` and `docs/design/agentic-dev-loop.md` (§1.1, lines 79-91) were all updated on this branch; this top-level design doc was not, so the repo now states both contracts. Nothing mechanical catches it: the design-doc lane only checks that backticked paths resolve, not prose. Fix belongs in the doc, not the new code.

samples.summary: The local carry-forward projection passes `mergedFrom` (and raw `severity`) through unprojected, diverging from the cloud copy it claims to mirror
samples.evidence: `carryForwardFindings` documents "PROJECT, never spread" and the new drift guard (`scripts/agent/prior-findings.test.mjs:~470`) only pins the two SELECTION filters. But the cloud copy it mirrors, `.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:1028`, projects each merged wording too — `mergedFrom: f.mergedFrom.slice(0,5).map((m) => ({ severity: norm(m.severity), summary: trim(m.summary,500), adjudication: … }))` — and normalizes severity (`severity: norm(f.severity)`), whereas `scripts/agent/prior-findings.mjs:174` carries `f.mergedFrom` verbatim and `f.severity` raw. `mergedFrom` entries are model output that reaches downstream prompt builders (`scripts/agent/review-panel.mjs:2896` folds them into the adjudication/verifier input; `scripts/agent/fix-brief.mjs` renders merged wordings in the checklist — see `scripts/agent/fix-brief.test.mjs:140`), so locally an arbitrary-key, unbounded-length nested object rides into the next round's prompt where the cloud path would have trimmed and rebuilt it. Still works today (the local loop has no fixer and `normalizeSeverity` is applied downstream), but it is the same silent-divergence failure the extraction and its drift guard exist to prevent.

finding.summary: `--fresh` deletes every round directory BEFORE the new bound refusal runs, so the refusal it added is both destructive and self-disarming
finding.evidence: scripts/agent/spec-to-pr.mjs:954-958 does the `rmSync` of every `round-N` directory whenever `args.fresh && !dryRun`. The new bound check the delta introduces only runs afterwards, at scripts/agent/spec-to-pr.mjs:974-983. So `spec-to-pr.mjs review --fresh` on a branch at MAX_SELF_REVIEW_ROUNDS: (1) deletes all three rounds' `verdict.json` files, then (2) prints "…discarding their verdicts is not converging, it is forgetting" and exits 1 — having already discarded them; and (3) the very next `review --fresh` (or a plain `review`) sees an empty base, so `roundsOnDisk(base)` at scripts/agent/spec-to-pr.mjs:949 returns [], `spentRound` is 1, `roundBoundNotice` is "", and the round runs with no carry-forward and no `--force`. The guard is bypassed by running the same refused command twice, and the carry-forward store is destroyed on the refusal path. The delta newly makes this reachable: before it, `--fresh` always renumbered to 1 and the bound never fired on this path. The new CLI test only exercises `--dry-run` (scripts/agent/spec-to-pr.test.mjs:703-744), where the delete is skipped, so it cannot see this. Fix belongs on the new code: move the `spentRound`/`notice` refusal above the `--fresh` delete block.

verdict.reason: The finding's core factual claim — that the `--fresh` `rmSync` runs before the new round-bound refusal — is false in this working tree. The only round-directory deletion in the file is at spec-to-pr.mjs:988-992 (`if (args.fresh && !dryRun) { ... rmSync(path.join(base, name), ...) }`), and it is preceded by the bound refusal at spec-to-pr.mjs:966-975, which computes `spentRound` from `onDiskBefore` (read at :949, before any mutation) and `return fail(...)`s with the "discarding their verdicts is not converging, it is forgetting" message. A `Grep` for `rmSync` across the file yields only the import (:44), two comment mentions (:723, :930) and the single call at :990 — nothing at the claimed :954-958, which is a comment plus `const onDisk = args.fresh ? [] : onDiskBefore;`. Consequently the refusal is inert on disk, and the alleged "run it twice and the second sees an empty base" bypass cannot occur: the verdicts survive, so the next `roundsOnDisk(base)` still reports three spent rounds and the bound fires again. The claim that only a `--dry-run` test covers this is also wrong: spec-to-pr.test.mjs:746-781 executes a real (non-dry-run) `review --fresh`, asserts the failure, and then asserts all three `round-N/security/verdict.json` files still exist (:774-777). The fix the finding asks for is already the shipped ordering.
